followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability and task-preference fit.

On **capability**, Willet leads across the relevant benchmarks — MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 75.4), GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs 55.6), and Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 82.7). Your query is essentially conceptual explanation plus applied reasoning about microeconomics, which is exactly what those benchmarks measure. Those gaps are well outside run-to-run variance, so Willet should give a sharper, more accurate breakdown.

On **task preference**, Dunlin's distinctive strengths — a steep appetite for open-ended creative invention and an aversion to harm-adjacent or hostile content — simply don't apply here. Your request is friendly, warm, and entirely benign, so Dunlin's aversions never come into play, and while it likes generative novelty, an explanatory econ question isn't really open-ended invention. So neither of Dunlin's preference advantages gives it an edge for this task.

With preferences roughly neutral between them, the decision came down to capability, and Willet wins that comfortably.
